transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Well… it’s my eating, I suppose. Sometimes when I start on certain comfort foods, I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but… my hand just keeps going back, like I can’t quite make myself stop.
How often do these episodes of eating more than you intended happen?

Most weeks, I’d say. Not every day or anything… usually maybe once or twice, especially on those quiet afternoons after choir or working in the garden. It’s been more like that since my friend passed.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating more than you intended?
Yes… I do. I feel ashamed afterward, and sad. Like I’ve taken something that used to feel like family and caring, and turned it into something I need to hide from folks at church.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself much. My clothes feel about the same, I think… nothing I’d call a big change.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing something to counteract the calories?
I don’t think so… I mean, I don’t really do anything special afterward. I just feel bad and try to move on.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… no, I don’t make myself throw up.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics after eating?
Not really… I don’t use things like that after eating.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two, and feel like you can't stop?
Yes… sometimes. It’s mostly with comfort food. Once I start, I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but then my hand just keeps going back, like I can’t quite stop myself.
Have these episodes of eating more than you intended been happening for more than three months?
About three months, yes… it started after my close friend passed away. Since then, it’s been happening.
On average, how many times a week do you have these episodes where you eat more than you intended and feel like you can't stop?
Most weeks… maybe once or twice. It tends to be in the quiet afternoons, after choir or when I’ve been out gardening. Since my friend passed, that’s when it’s been happening.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake after one of these episodes of eating more than you intended?
No… I don’t think so. I don’t usually skip meals on purpose after.
Do you usually eat these comfort foods when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or sad?
I’m not really sure… maybe sometimes. I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s stress or sadness exactly.
Do you think eating these comfort foods helps you feel better when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or sad?
I don’t really know. Maybe for a little while it does, but I haven’t thought about it that way much.
Do you think eating these comfort foods is a way for you to deal with difficult emotions?
I’m not sure. I guess it could be sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it that way. It’s just… something I do, I suppose.
Do you think eating these comfort foods is a way for you to cope with feeling sad about your friend's passing?
I don’t know… maybe. I haven’t really connected it that way. It’s hard to say.
Do you think eating these comfort foods helps you avoid thinking about your friend who passed away?
I’m not really sure. I guess I don’t think about it like that… it’s just something I end up doing sometimes.
Do you think eating these comfort foods is a way for you to deal with feeling sad or upset about things other than your friend's passing?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid much attention to that. Sometimes I just eat what’s there, I guess… I’m not sure it’s because I’m upset.
Do you think eating these comfort foods is a way for you to deal with feelings of sadness or upset in general?
I’m not sure… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really think of it that way. I haven’t noticed a clear reason, I guess.
Do you think eating these comfort foods is usually in response to feeling emotional?
I don’t know if I’d say usually. I haven’t really noticed it that way… sometimes I just eat, and I don’t think much about why.
Do you think you eat these comfort foods because you're feeling emotional?
I don’t really know. I guess it could be sometimes, but I don’t pay that much attention to it. I just… eat what sounds good, and that’s about all I can say.
